results.note: native_macd_oracle (tests/test_differential.py:33-54) and native_stochrsi_oracle (:57-91) each wrap the real talib.MACD/STOCHRSI/RSI C functions with unittest.mock.patch.object(..., wraps=...) and assert call_count == 0 after invoking pandas_ta with talib=False — a hard runtime check that delegation didn't happen, not merely trusting the passed argument.

Deliberately sets talib_enabled=True (so pandas_ta.macd delegates to the real talib.MACD) and asserts the guard's AssertionError actually fires with message 'oracle delegated to TA-Lib' — proves the call_count==0 guard bites on a genuine delegation rather than being a no-op assertion. Only demonstrated for MACD, not a mirrored control for StochRSI, but the mechanism (and criterion) is generic.

CONVERGED_TAIL_LENGTH=32 bars sliced from the end of a 500-bar synthetic series for both MACD (lines 98-113) and StochRSI (lines 142-157) comparisons, well past each indicator's warmup (~35 bars for MACD(12,26,9), ~31 for StochRSI(14,14,3)) — leading bars are excluded from both oracle and actual arrays.

The diff adds only two free-floating YAML comment lines to registry.yaml (lines 6-7); no IndicatorDefinition entry for MACD or STOCHRSI was added despite ingest/registry.py already reserving RECURSIVE_TALIB_FUNCTIONS={'RSI','ATR','EMA','STOCHRSI','MACD'} and a talib_function/parameters schema for exactly this purpose (ingest/registry.py:26,58-59,84-90). The 'registry' test (tests/test_differential.py:160-168) just does REGISTRY_PATH.read_text() and asserts a hardcoded string is a substring of the raw file — it never loads/validates via load_registry()/IndicatorRegistry, and nothing cross-checks the comment against indicators.py's actual default parameters. This is a criterion satisfied by a comment, not a genuine registry assertion.

Numerically proves ingest/indicators.py's stochrsi() (which returns TA-Lib's fastd, ingest/indicators.py:86-93) matches the independent pandas-ta-classic oracle's first/K column within 1e-6 on the converged tail — real evidence that TA-Lib's fastd equals TradingView's K, backed also by the function's docstring ('Return TradingView-style StochRSI K for the newest bar.', ingest/indicators.py:83), so a reader comparing the returned value to a TradingView chart's K line is not misled into thinking it's D.
Named gate `uv run pytest tests/test_differential.py -q --no-header -o addopts= --tb=short` exited 0, confirming the file runs standalone.

note: 5 of 6 criteria hold up under inspection with real, non-tautological tests (mocked TA-Lib call-count guards that actually fire, tail-only comparisons past warmup, and a genuine numeric proof that TA-Lib's fastd equals TradingView's K). C4 is gamed: the 'registry' assertion is just a substring check against two comment lines bolted onto registry.yaml — no structured IndicatorDefinition/talib_function entry for MACD or STOCHRSI was added to the actual validated registry, even though the schema (ingest/registry.py) already anticipates exactly that.
